title: Feature file v2.11.0
description: `features/<name>/feature.json`: the committed assignment `workflow launch <name>` prepares. `workers` declares every lane: a node id that must match a `workers[].node_id` of the policy file and the task file that lane receives. `launch --workers a,b` selects a subset; omitted means every declared lane. 2.1.0 adds the optional `reviewers`: every reviewer of the run with its brief (a file relative to the feature directory, existing and non-empty, or `builtin:<id>` for a brief bundled in `workflow/prompts/reviewers/`); a file without `reviewers` runs the single built-in reviewer (`workflow/prompts/review.md`) with id `review`. A 1.0.0 file (`ui_task`/`adapter_task`) is refused by `launch` with a message to use 2.x. Hand-written; the controller validates it with `workflow.verification.validate_schema("feature", ...)` and additionally requires unique node ids, the same id set as the policy, existing non-empty task and brief files inside the feature directory, unique reviewer ids that are neither a lane id nor a reserved name, and version 2.1.0 or later whenever `reviewers` is present. 2.2.0 turns on the guardrails (docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md section 4.3): every task must have non-empty `## Goal`, `## Acceptance` and `## Stop` sections, the feature directory must hold a non-empty `decisions.md`, and `prd` must exist in the target; it adds the optional `challenge` (default true: a design challenge runs before any worker) and `prd`. 2.3.0 keeps every 2.2.0 guardrail and adds the optional `sidecar` (docs/PRD_REVIEW_SIDECAR.md section 3): a review sidecar that reads the lanes' diffs and panes on a cadence and on every claimed completion during the work phase, keeps `<run>/sidecar.ledger.json` (contracts/workflow/sidecar.schema.json) and may message a lane through the controller; `false` or an absent key means none, and `sidecar` on an earlier version is refused. `launch` additionally requires a `prompt` file inside the feature directory that exists and is not empty, or a `builtin:<id>` bundled in `workflow/prompts/sidecar/`. 2.4.0 keeps every 2.3.0 rule and adds the optional `critical` (default false), which the workflow-grill skill sets when the operator confirms that the feature's code is critical: an automatic run then stops after review for the operator's `approve`, under any profile; `critical` on an earlier version is refused. 2.4.0 also adds the optional `tryout` (default false): a user-facing feature the operator tries before the merge to main, and that counts toward the untried-feature limit; `tryout` on an earlier version is refused. 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 files launch as before, with a note that no guardrail is enforced; 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 files launch unchanged. 2.5.0 keeps every 2.4.0 rule and adds the optional `attack` (docs/PRD_ATTACK_PASS.md section 3). 2.6.0 keeps every 2.5.0 rule and adds the optional `panels` (docs/PRD_MULTI_PROVIDER_PANEL.md section 3): report-only multi-provider panels, one per stage, each with its providers (`claude` or `pi`), brief, requirements, budget, timeout and overlap threshold; `panels` on an earlier version is refused, as is a panel whose `report_only` is not true, a `pi` provider without a `provider/id` model, a `deepseek/*` provider without the key guard, and (this slice) a `challenge`-stage panel. 2.7.0 keeps every 2.6.0 rule and adds the optional per-lane `workers[].model` and `workers[].effort`: that lane's worker runs them instead of the run-wide worker pin (prepare records every lane's effective pin as plan.nodes[<lane>].roles); the judges never take them, and either field on an earlier version is refused. 2.8.0 keeps every 2.7.0 rule and adds the optional per-lane `workers[].skills` (docs/PRD_WORKER_SKILLS.md section 3): 1 to 8 unique names, each matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; that lane's worker and every repair session launch without --safe-mode, with --setting-sources "", --plugin-dir <run>/skills/<lane> and the Skill tool, loading those skills and nothing else of the operator's customizations (prepare copies each named ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ into the run and pins its digest); `skills` on an earlier version is refused, and a lane without it launches exactly as today. 2.9.0 keeps every 2.8.0 rule and adds the optional `critique` (docs/PRD_USER_CRITIQUE.md section 3): the critique reviewer, a controller-owned headless Claude job that uses the frozen candidate's running app as a user; `critique` on an earlier version is refused, a feature that declares it must name a policy `critique_app` (policy 1.4.0), the reviewer id `critique` and the prefix `critique-` are reserved, and a feature that declares `critique` may not have a lane named `critique`. A 2.9.0 feature without `critique` launches byte for byte as a 2.8.0 one. 2.10.0 keeps every 2.9.0 rule and adds the optional per-lane `workers[].lane_review` (docs/PRD_LANE_REVIEWER.md section 3): 1 to 4 reviewers (`{transport claude|pi, model?, effort?}`, distinct by model) that review that lane's diff after it passes verification, with `rounds` (0..2, default 1), `timeout_minutes` (1..30, default 10) and `budget_usd` (0.5..20, default 3); a P0/P1 from any reviewer starts one fix round of that lane through the repair loop before the candidate (the record is never a gate when the plan is not automatic or `--fix-rounds` is 0). `lane_review` on an earlier version is refused, and a lane without it runs exactly as today. 2.11.0 keeps every 2.10.0 rule and adds the judged review panel (features/review-panel-registry/prd.md section 6): a `panels[]` entry with `report_only: false`, closed keys `{id, stage: review, report_only: false, seats?, prompt?, requirements?, judge?}`, whose seats are 1 to 16 names from the shared reviewer list (contracts/workflow/reviewers.schema.json; absent means every enabled entry), whose default brief (`builtin:review` or no prompt) is workflow/prompts/panels/review-judged.md, and whose `judge` takes `timeout_minutes` 5..60 (default 30) and `budget_usd` 1..50 (default 15). One Claude judge rules on every finding of the seats and the built-in reviewers. A judged panel has no `providers`, `overlap_threshold`, `budget_usd` or `timeout_minutes`; it is refused below 2.11.0, at `stage: challenge`, twice, beside any other panel, and without `launch --judge-model`. Report-only panels keep their 2.6.0 form at 2.11.0.

policy.description: Policy file relative to the feature directory (contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json).

node_id.description: A lane id as the policy declares it: lower-case, at most 32 characters, never a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix. The lane id `critique` is reserved only in a feature that declares `critique` (refused at launch and prepare, PRD 4.7), so a feature before 2.9.0 keeps it.

task.description: Task file relative to the feature directory.

model.description: 2.7.0: this lane's worker model (`claude --model`), pinned at prepare as plan.nodes[<lane>].roles; omitted means the run-wide worker model (--worker-model, default claude-opus-4-8). Refused on an earlier version. Never a judge's.

effort.description: 2.7.0: this lane's worker effort (`claude --effort`), pinned at prepare as plan.nodes[<lane>].roles; omitted means the run-wide worker effort (--worker-effort, else WORKFLOW_WORKER_EFFORT). Refused on an earlier version. Never a judge's.

skills.description: 2.8.0: 1 to 8 unique Claude Code skills this lane's worker and repair sessions load (docs/PRD_WORKER_SKILLS.md section 3). Each name resolves to ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ on the controller's host, copied into <run>/skills/<lane> and pinned by digest; the lane launches without --safe-mode, with --setting-sources "", --plugin-dir and the Skill tool. Refused on an earlier version. Never a judge's, and the print transport cannot load them.

lane_review.description: 2.10.0: this lane's own reviewers (docs/PRD_LANE_REVIEWER.md section 3). After the lane passes verification they review its diff in parallel; a P0/P1 from any one starts one fix round of the lane through the repair loop before the candidate. Pinned at prepare as plan.nodes[<lane>].lane_review with the bundled brief's text and sha256 and the proved pi bin. Refused on an earlier version.

reviewers.description: 1 to 4 reviewers, distinct by model, each a panel provider: {transport (claude|pi), model?, effort?}. A pi provider needs a provider/id model; effort applies to a claude provider only.

rounds.description: Fix rounds this lane may get from its reviewers (default 1; 0 is review-only), separate from --fix-rounds.

budget_usd.description: Per-reviewer budget (default 3), passed as the claude transport's --max-budget-usd; pi is bounded by timeout only.

reviewers.description: 2.1.0: the reviewers the review node launches in parallel over the same candidate, in declared order. Each reviewer owns the node `review-<reviewer_id>` and the files `review-<reviewer_id>.*`.

reviewer_id.description: Lower-case, at most 32 characters, unique, never a lane id of the policy nor a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix. The reviewer id `critique` is refused only in a feature that declares `critique` (the critique reviewer owns that id, PRD 4.2), so a feature before 2.9.0 keeps it.

prompt.description: Brief file relative to the feature directory, or `builtin:<id>` for a bundled brief (workflow/prompts/reviewers/<id>.md); it replaces the built-in brief and states only what to look for (the controller appends the bundle paths, task locations, lane vocabulary and completion protocol).

challenge.description: 2.2.0: run the design challenge node before any worker launch (default true). `false` records the challenge as disabled and the run's graph has no challenge node.

prd.description: 2.2.0: the specification the design challenge reads, a path relative to the target repository that must exist.

critical.description: 2.4.0: the operator confirmed at the grill that this feature's code is critical (default false). `true` pins an automatic run's finish to `approval`: it stops after review until the operator approves.

tryout.description: 2.4.0: a user-facing feature the operator tries before the merge to main (default false). `true` pins `plan.tryout` at prepare: each integrated run waits for `python -m workflow tryout <run> --result works|broken|skipped --by operator`, and a new tryout launch stops while 3 other features wait for theirs (`--allow-untried "<reason>" --by operator` overrides).

attack.description: 2.5.0: the attack pass (docs/PRD_ATTACK_PASS.md section 3). `false` (or no key) means none; `attack` on an earlier version is refused. One `claude --print` attacker runs per angle at the review step over the frozen candidate, proving each stated requirement that does not hold with a failing test; the controller re-runs each test and a skeptic judges it. Report-only. The bounds are pinned into `plan.attack` at prepare with the defaults shown.

angles.description: 1 to 3 distinct angles; one attacker runs per angle.

requirements.description: 0 to 10 distinct repository-relative paths of the project's requirements documents; given to the attacker and the skeptic beside the PRD. A path outside the repository is refused, as the PRD is. Launch refuses a path not committed at HEAD.

sidecar.description: 2.3.0: the review sidecar. `false` (or no key) means none. The bounds are pinned into `plan.sidecar` at prepare with the defaults shown: one pass every `cadence_seconds` and at once when a lane writes a `completed` completion, each a read-only `claude --print` job stopped after `pass_timeout_seconds`, at most `max_passes` passes plus the final pass, and at most `max_messages_per_lane` messages typed into each lane's pane.

prompt.description: The brief: a file relative to the feature directory (existing, non-empty) or `builtin:<id>` for a brief bundled in `workflow/prompts/sidecar/` (today `senior-review`). The controller appends the run's vocabulary, the pass inputs, the ledger and the output rules.

panels.description: 2.6.0: the multi-provider panels (docs/PRD_MULTI_PROVIDER_PANEL.md section 3), one instance per stage. Each runs every `providers[]` entry over one assembled context file at its stage, records each provider's findings in `<run>/panel.json` (contracts/workflow/panel.schema.json) annotated with cross-provider overlap, and never changes the run's verdict. Pinned into `plan.panels` at prepare with the defaults shown. `panels` on an earlier version is refused. 2.11.0 adds the judged review panel (`report_only: false`), alone in its feature.

stage.description: Where the panel runs. This slice runs `review` only; `challenge` is refused at launch until the follow-up slice.

model.description: Required for `pi`, of the form provider/id (openai-codex/gpt-6-sol); optional for `claude` (else the judges' pin).

effort.description: A claude provider's --effort, replacing the judges' pin; refused for `pi`.

providers.description: 1 to 4 providers, distinct by model (or by transport for a default claude).

prompt.description: The brief: a file relative to the feature directory, or `builtin:<stage>` (workflow/prompts/panels/<stage>.md).

requirements.description: 0 to 10 distinct repository-relative paths of requirement documents, pinned at prepare and placed in the context file.

budget_usd.description: The claude provider's --max-budget-usd; informational for pi.

timeout_minutes.description: Each provider job's bound from its own launch.

overlap_threshold.description: A finding is accepted when at least N providers raised it, or every configured provider for "all" (1 accepts any).

report_only.description: Must be true in v1: the panel never blocks or changes the verdict.

stage.description: A judged panel runs at the review stage only (the design-challenge panel is step 2).

report_only.description: false: a judged panel, whose findings go to the judge with the built-in reviewers'.

seats.description: Reviewer names from the shared reviewer list (never inline entries); absent means every enabled entry, in list order.

prompt.description: The seats' brief: a file relative to the feature directory, or `builtin:review` (the default), which a judged panel resolves to workflow/prompts/panels/review-judged.md.

requirements.description: 0 to 10 distinct repository-relative paths of requirement documents, pinned at prepare and placed in the context file.

judge.description: The judge's bounds; its model is the run's --judge-model and its effort high.

critique.description: 2.9.0: the critique reviewer (docs/PRD_USER_CRITIQUE.md sections 3-6). `false` (or no key) means none; `critique` on an earlier version is refused, and a feature that declares it needs the policy's `critique_app` (policy 1.4.0). A controller-owned headless `claude --print --json-schema` job runs at the review step in a disposable worktree of the frozen candidate: it starts the app on free ports, uses it as a user to walk each named lane's `## Goal` and `verify_yourself` line and runs the Impeccable critique, then returns structured findings the controller turns into a reviewer decision (reviewer id `critique`). Its open P1 findings block the review and feed the fix loop exactly as another reviewer's do; the export carries each finding's steps and screenshots. Pinned into `plan.critique` at prepare.

lanes.description: 1 or more of the feature's lanes whose UI the critique walks; only these may be named in a finding's `worker`. Prepare pins the intersection with the selected lanes and refuses an empty one.

skills.description: The skills the critique job loads (feature.json 2.8.0 mechanism), pinned at prepare with digests under plan.critique.skills. Default ["impeccable"].

max_budget_usd.description: The job's --max-budget-usd, so a round's spend is capped (default 15).

timeout_minutes.description: The job's own deadline from its launch (default 45); past it the job is stopped and recorded as a failed critique.
